passages.note: Bill status page lists Martinez as a Co-Sponsor of HB 2853, the Arizona ESA expansion bill the Governor signed on 2022-07-07.
House Third Reading roll call shows a divided, non-near-unanimous final-passage vote on the single-subject ESA bill, with Martinez voting Y.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: The enacted text adds a catch-all qualified-student category covering any resident eligible for preschool-disability, kindergarten, or grades 1-12, making ESA eligibility effectively universal, while the unchanged qualified-school definition covers any nongovernmental school without excluding religious ones.

rows.reasoning: As a State Representative within her 2021-2023 term, Martinez co-sponsored and voted Y (Passed 31-26-3-0-0) on HB 2853 (2022), a single-subject ESA bill whose new qualified-student category admits any resident eligible for preschool-disability, kindergarten, or grades 1-12, making eligibility effectively universal and matching rung 5, "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family."
